chunks: Muhammad ibn ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahboub from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left his father, and his uncle, and his grandfather. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The father blocks the grandfather. The inheritance is for the father and there is nothing for the uncle and the grandfather'.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits when a man dies leaving his father, uncle, and grandfather?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'hijab al-awlawiyya' (blocking by priority), establishing that the father’s presence completely excludes the paternal grandfather from inheritance, a ruling distinct from some Sunni schools where they may share. It further clarifies that the paternal uncle is also excluded in this specific configuration, reinforcing the father's status as the primary male ascendant heir. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for resolving conflicts between close male relatives in the 'Asabaat' (residuary heirs) category.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who died and left his father, and his uncle, and his grandfather. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The father blocks the grandfather. The inheritance is for the father and there is nothing for the uncle and the grandfather’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who dies and leaves behind his father, his uncle and grandfather. He (the Imam) said, ‘The father bars the grandfather. The legacy belongs to the father and there is nothing for the uncle and grandfather.’”
